phenomena.what: Large numbers group by thousands: أَلْف 1,000, مِلْيُون 1,000,000, مِلْيَار 10⁹. 'Thousand' has a dual أَلْفَانِ and a plural آلَاف, and is counted like any noun.
phenomena.gap: أَلْف is taught; مِلْيُون and مِلْيَار are not lexemes, and numbers above 1000 are not practised.

phenomena.title: The clock: 'and a half', 'less a quarter'
phenomena.what: The time is the hour as a feminine ordinal plus a fraction: وَالنِّصْفُ 'and the half', وَالرُّبْعُ 'and the quarter', إِلَّا رُبْعًا 'less a quarter'; 'half past two' counts from the hour just passed.

model.other: نِصْف and رُبْع are lexemes (cr.04) with construct cells (نِصْفَ سَاعَةٍ).

phenomena.gap: إِلَّا (in إِلَّا رُبْعًا “a quarter to”) is not a lexeme, so no bank sentence shows it; it is taught in fn.ordinals.

NOUN.title: gender
NOUN.why: Drives the agreement of adjectives, verbs and pronouns and the polarity of the numbers 3–10.

NOUN.title: transliteration
NOUN.why: Shows the vowels and the sounds until the script is read fluently: the pausal form, without case or tanwīn ending (kitāb, muḥāmī, maqhā).

NOUN.title: root (radicals)
NOUN.why: Links the word to its family and to the dictionary; “none” for loanwords and for phrases (their parts have their own roots).

NOUN.title: pattern (wazn)
NOUN.why: The measure in ف ع ل letters (mafʿal = place, mifʿāl = tool, fāʿil = doer …) lets the learner guess new words; “none” for loanwords, phrases and words that fit no measure.

NOUN.title: sun letter (al- assimilates)
NOUN.why: With a sun letter the l of the article is not pronounced and the letter is doubled: الشَّمْسُ aš-šams; with a moon letter: الْقَمَرُ al-qamar.

NOUN.title: human (agreement class)
NOUN.why: Plurals of people agree in the plural; all other plurals agree as feminine singular (الْكُتُبُ جَدِيدَةٌ).

NOUN.title: plurals
NOUN.why: The plural is learned with the noun: its kind (broken, sound masculine -ūna, sound feminine -āt), its pattern and declension, and the meanings it belongs to (بُيُوت houses / أَبْيَات verses). “none” for mass nouns, names and words used only in the singular.

NOUN.title: dual
NOUN.why: Mostly regular (-āni), but ة becomes ت (سَنَتَانِ) and some duals are irregular (أَبَوَانِ); “none” for mass nouns, names and plural-only words.

NOUN.title: declension (of the singular; of the head noun in a phrase)
NOUN.why: Triptotes take tanwīn and -i in the genitive; diptotes (names, أَفْعَل, -ān, many broken plurals) take no tanwīn and -a; defective nouns end in -in (مُحَامٍ); invariable nouns never change (مَقْهًى، كُوسَا).

NOUN.title: unit noun
NOUN.why: One piece of a collective (تُفَّاحَة from تُفَّاح); needed for counting.

NOUN.title: forms of one meaning only
NOUN.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

ADJ.title: transliteration
ADJ.why: Shows the vowels: the pausal masculine singular (kabīr, ġālī).

ADJ.title: root (radicals)
ADJ.why: Links the adjective to the verb and the noun of the same family; “none” for adjectives made from loanwords.

ADJ.title: pattern (wazn)
ADJ.why: faʿīl, fāʿil, faʿlān, afʿal (colours), nisba -ī …; “none” when no measure applies.

ADJ.title: sun letter (al- assimilates)
ADJ.why: With a sun letter the l of the article is not pronounced and the letter is doubled: الشَّمْسُ aš-šams; with a moon letter: الْقَمَرُ al-qamar.

ADJ.title: made from
ADJ.why: A participle of a verb (بَارِد ← بَرَدَ), a nisba in -ī (بُنِّيّ ← بُنّ) or an elative; “none” for a basic adjective.

ADJ.title: feminine form
ADJ.why: Regular -a (كَبِيرَة), but فَعْلَاء for colours (حَمْرَاء) and فَعْلَى for faʿlān (عَطْشَى).

ADJ.title: masculine plural
ADJ.why: Broken or sound -ūna, for masculine plurals of people (non-human plurals usually take the feminine singular, though broken plurals also go with things: لَيَالٍ طِوَالٌ); some meanings have their own plural (كِبَار big / كُبَرَاء great men).

ADJ.title: declension (masculine singular)
ADJ.why: Colours (أَحْمَرُ) and faʿlān (عَطْشَانُ) are diptotes; غَالٍ is defective.

ADJ.title: comparative / superlative (elative)
ADJ.why: أَكْبَرُ from كَبِير; “none” when the comparison is made with أَكْثَرُ / أَشَدُّ + a maṣdar (colours, nisbas, participles).

ADJ.title: forms of one meaning only
ADJ.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

VERB.title: transliteration
VERB.why: Shows the vowels of the 3rd person singular past (the citation form).

VERB.title: root (radicals)
VERB.why: The verb is the centre of its word family.

VERB.title: root class
VERB.why: Weak radicals (و ي), a doubled radical or hamza change the conjugation: hollow قَالَ، defective مَشَى، assimilated وَصَلَ، doubled أَحَبَّ، hamzated أَكَلَ.

VERB.title: verb form
VERB.why: Form I … X gives the present, participle and maṣdar patterns and a typical meaning.

VERB.title: present (imperfect) 3rd person singular
VERB.why: The second principal part: the stem vowel of form I (يَكْتُبُ / يَشْرَبُ / يَجْلِسُ) cannot be predicted. “none” for a verb that has no present.

VERB.title: verbal noun (maṣdar)
VERB.why: Arabic’s “infinitive” (to eat = أَكْل); unpredictable for form I. “none” for a verb that has none.

VERB.title: active / passive participle
VERB.why: Very frequent as nouns and adjectives (كَاتِب writer, مَكْتُوب written); the passive participle only for verbs with an object.

VERB.title: object and preposition
VERB.why: What the verb takes: a direct object (accusative) or a preposition (ذَهَبَ إِلَى، خَرَجَ مِنْ، اِنْتَظَرَ + acc.), per meaning. “none” for a verb used without an object.

VERB.title: forms of one meaning only
VERB.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

ADV.title: transliteration
ADV.why: Shows the vowels; adverbs in -an keep the ending, which is part of the word.

ADV.title: root (radicals)
ADV.why: Links the adverb to its family; “none” for particles and phrases.

ADV.title: made from
ADV.why: Most adverbs are accusatives of nouns or adjectives (كَثِيرًا ← كَثِير، صَبَاحًا ← صَبَاح) or a preposition + a word (بِخَيْرٍ); “none” for a basic particle (هُنَا، الْآنَ).

ADV.title: forms of one meaning only
ADV.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

ADP.title: transliteration
ADP.why: Shows the vowels of the preposition.

ADP.title: written attached
ADP.why: بِـ and لِـ are written together with the next word; the others stand alone.

ADP.title: root (radicals)
ADP.why: The prepositions that are nouns (ẓarf) have a root (قَبْلَ ← ق ب ل); the short particles (فِي، مِنْ) have none.

ADP.title: kind of preposition
ADP.why: A true preposition (ḥarf: فِي، مِنْ، إِلَى), a noun in the accusative used as a preposition (ẓarf: قَبْلَ، عِنْدَ، أَمَامَ — it can itself follow مِنْ: مِنْ عِنْدِ), or a preposition + noun (phrase: بِدُونِ، بِجَانِبِ). All take the genitive.

ADP.title: forms of one meaning only
ADP.why: A form (a fixed phrase, another maṣdar, an adverbial accusative …) that belongs to one meaning of the word; “none” when every meaning has the same forms. Per-meaning plurals are in plurals.

PRON.title: person, number, gender
PRON.why: Gender in the 2nd and 3rd person (أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ، هُمْ / هُنَّ).

PRON.title: attached form
PRON.why: The pronoun as an ending on nouns, verbs and prepositions (كِتَابُكَ، يَرَاهُ، لَهَا).

NUM.title: transliteration
NUM.why: Shows the vowels of the citation form.

NUM.title: root (radicals)
NUM.why: The numbers are native words with roots (ث ل ث، ع ش ر); “none” for the compound numbers 11–19.

NUM.title: gender polarity
NUM.why: 3–10 (and the units of 13–19) take the form of the opposite gender: ثَلَاثَةُ كُتُبٍ but ثَلَاثُ سَيَّارَاتٍ.

NUM.title: the counted noun
NUM.why: The case and number of the noun with the number.

NUM.title: ordinal
NUM.why: The ordinal (masculine): ثَالِث from ثَلَاثَة; “first” is suppletive (أَوَّل); “none” for zero.

CCONJ.title: written attached
CCONJ.why: وَ and فَ are written together with the next word.

CCONJ.title: what follows
CCONJ.why: لٰكِنَّ takes a noun in the accusative or a pronoun suffix; the others join words or whole clauses.

SCONJ.title: what follows
SCONJ.why: أَنَّ / لِأَنَّ + an accusative noun or a pronoun suffix; أَنْ + a subjunctive verb; إِذَا + a past verb; عِنْدَمَا + a clause.

PART.title: written attached
PART.why: أَ is written together with the next word; the other particles stand alone.

INTJ.title: transliteration
INTJ.why: Shows the vowels of the formula.

INTJ.title: said to
INTJ.why: Many formulas change with the person addressed: a man, a woman, a group (كَيْفَ حَالُكَ / حَالُكِ / حَالُكُمْ).

INTJ.title: fixed answer
INTJ.why: The answer this formula gets (صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ → صَبَاحُ النُّورِ); “none” when there is no fixed answer.
